# THE BOUNDARY MANIFEST — every tracked JavaScript/TypeScript file, and what it is.
#
# One rule per line:  CLASS | pattern | reason | producer
#
#   CLASS     LOGIC (must become Rust, counted and capped) · BOUNDARY (a platform call, decides nothing)
#             · RENDERING (places what it was given) · GENERATED (a build step produces it)
#   pattern   repo-relative. A trailing `/` matches the whole tree; anything else is one exact file.
#             THE MOST SPECIFIC (LONGEST) MATCHING PATTERN WINS, so the order of these lines never decides.
#   reason    what it is, in one line — the thing a reviewer checks
#   producer  REQUIRED for GENERATED: the path of the thing that produces the file, checked to exist
#
# The gate is agent/tests/js_boundary_inventory.rs. LOGIC is the work that is left; its cap only falls.
#
# ── TWO RULES THAT MAKE THE HARD CASES A RULE RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT CALL ────────────────────────────────────
#
# A TEST BELONGS TO THE CODE IT TESTS. That is why `gateway/test/` is LOGIC — those files exercise the console
# worker's TypeScript and leave when it does — and why `agent/scripts/e2e/` is BOUNDARY: that suite drives the
# DEVICE's HTTP surface, whose subject is already Rust, so it is a harness rather than work that is left. A test
# whose subject is Rust is not a migration item; a test whose subject is JavaScript goes with its subject.
#
# A FIXTURE IS NOT A DECISION. `panel-stub.cjs` answers thirty comparisons and every one of them decides what the
# FAKE device returns — test data, not product behaviour. The same reading covers a probe SOURCE (it ships as text
# into a page), an assembler (a build step), and a harness renderer (it builds the surface under test). What makes
# a file LOGIC is that something the PRODUCT does depends on it.

# ── BOUNDARY: a platform call, and it decides nothing ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
BOUNDARY | agent/resources/panel-react/src/lib/ | the panel's data boundary — fetch, storage, DOM reads, and the seams that call the logic crate
BOUNDARY | agent/resources/panel-react/src/hooks/ | the panel's SSE/fetch hooks — a transport, not a decision
BOUNDARY | agent/resources/panel-react/src/wasm/panelLogic.ts | the hand-written seam onto the panel's logic crate
BOUNDARY | agent/resources/panel-react/scripts/ | the panel's CSS build tooling
BOUNDARY | gateway/ui/src/wasm/consoleLogic.ts | the hand-written seam onto the console's logic crate
BOUNDARY | gateway/ui/scripts/ | the console's build tooling
BOUNDARY | gateway/scripts/ | the console worker's build/deploy tooling
BOUNDARY | gateway/wasm/ | harnesses that execute the built JS+wasm worker and diff it against the shipping one
BOUNDARY | index/worker/ | the same harness shape for the index worker
BOUNDARY | index/landing/ | harnesses that render and verify the landing crate's output
BOUNDARY | index/spike-rust-landing/ | the landing spike's measure/verify harness
BOUNDARY | agent/summrise-workspace-dsh/ | the DSH plugin package — a plugin must be JS; the agent owns the connections
BOUNDARY | agent/summrise-cli/parity/ | the parity instrument — it runs the built CLI and the Rust binary and diffs their answers; it decides nothing about the product
BOUNDARY | agent/sweep-plan/parity/ | the parity instrument — it runs the PRE-CHANGE emitter, executes the payload it prints against a stub browser, and diffs that trace against the Rust plan; it decides nothing about the product
# ── AND THE THREE TOOLS ARE BOUNDARY, WHICH THE DIRECTORY RULE COULD NOT SEE (2026-10-09) ────────────────────
# `agent/scripts/` is LOGIC as a rule, and the audit of the sweeps named what stays inside it: the judge's
# JavaScript twin, the two payloads that drive and decide, the two small checkers, and the e2e suite. The three
# TOOLS were never in that list, and reading them line by line says why: each one dispatches on argv, FORWARDS
# `--passes` to the Rust plan without interpreting it, holds path constants and (for the landing) the fixture's
# URLs and page list, and assembles the emitted bundle through `lib/sweep-bundle.mjs`. The decisions they look
# like they make are all somewhere else — which plan runs (Rust), which passes it wants (Rust), what the verdict
# is (Rust). What they do is emit and dispatch, so they are the boundary the rest of this block is.
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/design-sweep.mjs | the shared collector and driver: the four probes as SOURCE STRINGS a browser evaluates, the passes that drive and measure, and the URL/escape helpers. It no longer formats anything — the acknowledgement notes moved to the judge (2026-10-09), which prints them before every exit
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/panel-design-sweep.mjs | the panel tool: argv dispatch, the in-page MOTION/TIMING probe SNIPPETS (strings a browser evaluates), the harness content stamp, and the emit through lib/sweep-bundle.mjs. It interprets no flag and decides no verdict
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/console-design-sweep.mjs | the console tool, the same shape: dispatch, `--passes` forwarded verbatim to the Rust plan, the entry stamp, the emit
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/landing-design-sweep.mjs | the landing tool: it RENDERS the surface under test (the fixture's URLs and page list) and emits it. Fixture data, not product behaviour
# AND THE SAME SPECIES, ONE LANDING LATER (landing 6): the policy's CASES are Rust now (summrise-url-policy
# src/tests.rs, 11 of them, ported case for case from the deleted test/url-policy.test.mjs), and what this
# file does is LOAD the committed wasm artifact in Node and call it — the one thing the Rust cases cannot
# do, because the shell's main process imports electron and no suite here can start it. It pins the
# exported surface, the boundary coercions a wasm `&str` parameter gets wrong, and the refusal shape; a
# harness that executes an artifact, exactly as gateway/wasm/verify.mjs is.
BOUNDARY | agent/summrise-desktop-electron/test/url-policy-wasm.test.mjs | it requires the built glue and executes the committed .wasm in Node; it decides nothing (the cases are Rust)
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/sweep-plan.mjs | the EMIT-TIME half of the plan: it runs `summrise-sweep-plan` and parses its stdout — one process call, no decision. The plan itself is Rust (agent/sweep-plan/)
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/sweep/plan-runtime.cjs | the PAYLOAD-side half: it turns a surface's fields into `page.setViewportSize` / `goto` / `emulateMedia` / `reload` and answers `wants(name)` from the plan's own map — platform calls, and it decides nothing (every boolean it reads is serialized by the Rust rather than defaulted here)
BOUNDARY | agent/src/plugins/playwright/helper.js | the page-side helper the playwright plugin drives
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/e2e/ | the device e2e bundle: the page-side half runs where browser_run_script runs
# ── AND THE SIX THE SWEEPS' AUDIT OF 2026-10-08 CLEARED, EACH BY READING ITS CONTROL FLOW RATHER THAN ITS NAME ──
# The audit was run because the paragraph that used to claim "everything left is a boundary" was written without one,
# and it retracted two of its own findings (see the spec's §4.1). These six are the part that survived: none of them
# decides anything the judge or the plan does not already own, and each names the platform call it makes.
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/sweep-bundle.mjs | the ASSEMBLER: it resolves each payload's requires and compiles what it returns, so a module that does not parse fails at the commit. A build step, and the emitter's own producer
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/contrast-probe.mjs | the in-page probe SOURCE — a template of code a browser evaluates to measure contrast. It ships as text into the page; the comparison against the requirement is what the payload still does in JS, and that is counted at the payload, not here
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/panel-render-audit.mjs | renders the harness HTML the sweep measures (and reads DECORATIVE_WAIVERS to label decorative rows in that fixture). It builds the surface under test
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/sweep/panel-stub.cjs | the STUB DEVICE: a fixture that answers the agent's API so the panel sweep can run with no device. Its thirty comparisons decide what the FAKE answers, which is test data rather than product behaviour
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/sweep/live-run.cjs | the live-panel program: it drives the panel the device is actually running and returns rows. One guard, no verdict
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/sweep/landing-run.cjs | a payload that drives a browser over one page and returns rows — measured: zero comparisons, and its two template literals are selectors
BOUNDARY | .agents/skills/setup-ts-deep-modules/ | a tooling config for the skill, not product code
BOUNDARY | docs/superpowers/p0/ | the P0 measurement harness — historical evidence, and a deletion candidate
BOUNDARY | proxies/api-relay/relay/ | the relay crate's own harness
BOUNDARY | proxies/summrise-relay/ | the retired relay worker's harness, kept for the differential

# ── LOGIC: the work that is left ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
LOGIC | agent/scripts/ | the design sweeps' driver and judge, plus the page-side payloads (landing 2)
LOGIC | scripts/test/ | six gates that spawn a toolchain (landing 3)
LOGIC | agent/summrise-agent-npm/src/ | the CLI's decisions (landing 4)
LOGIC | agent/summrise-agent-npm/test/ | the CLI's suite, ported with it (landing 4)
LOGIC | agent/summrise-desktop-electron/src/ | the Electron shell's remaining decisions — token/auth, the loopback control server, agent lifecycle, window policy. The URL/origin/cert policy LEFT this directory in landing 6 (agent/summrise-url-policy, wasm), so what is here is main.ts's host half and whatever main.ts still decides for itself
LOGIC | agent/summrise-desktop-electron/test/ | that shell's tests, ported with it (landing 6)
LOGIC | gateway/src/ | the console worker's entry and plugins — A6 (landing 5)
LOGIC | gateway/test/ | the console worker's suite (landing 5)
LOGIC | gateway/config/ | the provider catalogue as TypeScript, becoming data (B)
# ── THE INDEX'S JAVASCRIPT IS THE ORACLE, NOT WORK THAT IS LEFT (measured 2026-10-09) ─────────────────────────
# The index worker was cut over to Rust before this migration began, and these files were still counted as
# LOGIC on the assumption that their cutover was simply unharvested. Reading what depends on them says
# otherwise, and each dependency is named here because "delete the old implementation" was the wrong move:
#   * `index/worker/verify.mjs` drives `index/src/index.js` AS PUBLISHED, with stub bindings, and diffs status,
#     sorted headers and body bytes against the Rust — it is the differential, and deleting it deletes the proof.
#   * `agent/scripts/landing-design-sweep.mjs` does `import { PAGE } from "../../index/src/page.js"` — a LIVE
#     import by a tool that renders the page under test.
#   * `index/landing/verify.mjs` reads `page.js` out of a pinned commit with `git show <ref>:…`, so that file's
#     history is the reference the landing page is measured against.
# The Rust is what runs (`index/wrangler.jsonc` names `worker/build/index.js`, measured by fetching the deployed
# module from the API and finding the wasm glue in it), so nothing here decides product behaviour: these files
# exist to be COMPARED WITH, which is the boundary `agent/summrise-cli/parity/` and the sweeps' parity
# instrument are already classified as.
BOUNDARY | index/src/ | the ORACLE the Rust index worker is measured against (`verify.mjs` drives this entry with stub bindings; the landing sweep imports `PAGE` from `page.js`). The Rust is what runs
BOUNDARY | index/test/ | the oracle's own suite: it exercises the JavaScript the differential drives, and it leaves when the differential does — not when the worker does
BOUNDARY | proxies/api-relay/api/ | **THE RELAY'S ORACLE, NOT ITS LOGIC — AND CI SAYS SO IN ITS OWN WORDS.** ci.yml calls this suite "the ORACLE the committed fixture was generated from" (73 cases, its own `node --test` step), and three Rust gates read these files as TEXT: `agent/tests/proxy_timeout_parity.rs` and `proxy_cors_parity.rs` compare the Rust's timeout/header and CORS constants against `git.ts`/`github.ts`/`gform.ts`/`zen.js`/`proxy.js`, and `relay/tests/two_relays_agree.rs` reads `git.ts`/`github.ts` for the hosts and env-var names. `relay/differential.mjs` compares the two implementations' byte-for-byte answers on 14 requests, and that comparison needs both sides present. **The Rust relay is what serves**: nginx's `/api/` was pointed at `127.0.0.1:8082` on 2026-10-09 and proved by stopping the Node unit (the public endpoint still answered 401 with only the Rust one up). The Node bundle stays deployed as the one-line rollback, which is the second reason its source cannot leave. Deleting these files would delete the proof and the fallback, not the work — the work moved to `proxies/api-relay/relay/`, which the manifest already carries as BOUNDARY.
BOUNDARY | proxies/api-relay/server/ | the same oracle half, one layer up: `routing.mjs` is the pure URL routing + entry plumbing whose decisions moved to Rust first (`relay/src/`, covered by `cargo test --manifest-path proxies/api-relay/relay/Cargo.toml` in CI), and `entry.mjs` is what `build-relay.sh` stages into `dist/entry.mjs` for the differential and for the deployed rollback bundle. Its own suite (`server/test/`) is the oracle's proof, for the reason the paragraph above gives.
LOGIC | scripts/ | the root build/release tooling (landing 3)
